item.title: “Ashes To Go” Tradition Continues in Preston Center
item.description: A nearly decade-long tradition continued this week on Ash Wednesday as the faithful received ashes in Preston Center from Saint Michael and All Angels Episcopal Church.

item.title: DART Board OKs Plan That Would Return Some Sales Tax Dollars to Cities
item.description: The Dallas Area Rapid Transit (DART) board Friday greenlit a plan that could return some sales tax dollars to member cities in an effort to persuade cities — including Highland Park and University Park — to call off their withdrawal elections.

item.title: Playoffs Opening For Local Hoops Teams
item.description: It’s officially playoff time for local basketball programs competing in the UIL, while state championships are set to be decided this week for teams in TAPPS.

item.title: Maja Lardner Takes Goal-Scoring Prowess to NWSL
item.description: Maja Lardner admits she’s never been the best judge of her own talent. And until recently, she wasn’t sure whether professional soccer was in her future.

item.title: Groundhog Day Brought Changes for HPHS Sports Schedules
item.description: Highland Park discovered its future foes on the gridiron and hardwood Feb. 2 when the UIL unveiled new district alignments for the 2026-28 school years.

item.title: Loved LunarFest? Let Its Volunteers Know!
item.description: People Newspapers celebrated the Year of the Fire Horse on Feb. 21 at LunarFest, an event that brought together the traditions of the Chinese New Year, Korean Seollal, and Vietnamese Tết.

item.title: Preston Hollow Crime Reports Feb. 17-22
item.description: Multiple cars were broken into, and property was stolen in this week's crime reports.

item.title: Dallas ISD Launches Additional Days Calendar
item.description: The district has added an additional days school year calendar for 13 elementary schools and for sixth graders in seven middle schools so students can get extra support and spend time exploring activities that will enrich their school experience.

item.title: Donors Make $50M Gift to Boost SMU Athletics
item.description: A group of four families ponied up $50 million to boost student athletics by funding scholarships, Name Image and Likeness (NIL) advancement, and revenue sharing.
